Capability-by-capability comparison grounded in the implemented methodologies; claims restricted to features demonstrated in the repository record.
Natural language text. Paper 1 addresses natural-language text plagiarism only.
Hybrid lexical–semantic scoring: max(sublinear TF-IDF cosine, Sentence-BERT all-MiniLM-L6-v2 cosine); a single fixed threshold (tau=0.5000) categorizes pairs as direct copies vs. paraphrases.
column3: Calibrated multi-view scorer with predictive-entropy tri-band routing: low-risk pairs pruned at Stage-1, uncertain pairs escalated to a heavy verifier, high-risk pairs directly flagged for review.
column4: Proposed replaces static max() fusion and single-threshold decisions with a calibrated cascade that routes pairs adaptively; Paper 1 decides every pair exhaustively with one threshold.

column2: TF-IDF word n-gram vectors and 384-d Sentence-BERT dense embeddings (two views combined by max()).
column3: Twelve text views: TF-IDF lexical overlap, character 3-grams/LCS, MiniLM semantic embeddings, and structural stylometry (length, sentence count, type-token ratio), fused through a Platt-calibrated logistic scorer.
column4: Proposed fuses orthogonal views; Paper 1 combines two views with a brittle max() operator.

column4: Comparable lexical coverage; proposed screens lexically before any semantic escalation.

column4: Proposed quantifies decision uncertainty; Paper 1 does not.

column3: Calibrated posteriors with theta_low/theta_high gates; low-confidence pairs are escalated instead of forced to a binary decision.
column4: Proposed defers ambiguous cases; Paper 1 forces all pairs to an immediate binary verdict.

column2: Condition E1: none (all pairs scored). Condition E2: fixed dual-threshold routing with no budget formalization.
column3: Yes — budget-capped, recall-floored, entropy-driven Stage-2 escalation with an explicit computational budget.
column4: Proposed formalizes adaptive routing; Paper 1's E2 is only an informal fixed-band precursor.

column2: E2 reports ~30% workload reduction vs exhaustive SBERT (2.875 vs 4.163 ms/pair).
column3: 26.53% of pairs pruned at Stage-1; expensive calls reduced to 70.03% of pairs (29.97 percentage-point saving); latency 3.167 vs 4.143 ms/pair.
column4: Both reduce cost; proposed does so within a calibrated, budget-aware policy while retaining 85.98% candidate recall.

column2: No formal false-positive control; max() fusion can amplify correlated view errors; FPR 0.3552 on the test partition.
column3: High-risk gate theta_high targets precision; calibrated posteriors lower the false-positive rate (FPR 0.3170; specificity 0.6830 vs 0.6448).
column4: Proposed lowers false positives at the cost of some recall.

column2: Recall 0.8570: the semantic view catches paraphrase, but low-scoring plagiarized pairs are missed outright once scored below the threshold.
column3: Uncertain-band escalation retains candidates for heavy verification; candidate recall 0.8598 (about 14% of positives pruned at screening).
column4: Proposed trades a bounded amount of candidate recall for cost efficiency; Paper 1 retains all candidates but scores every pair expensively.

column2: SBERT forward pass on every pair (~4.16 ms/pair in E1) is expensive at cohort scale.
column3: Stage-1 resolves 26.53% of pairs at lexical cost; only the uncertain band consumes the SBERT budget.
column4: Proposed reduces per-pair cost; both remain transformer-dependent on retained pairs.

column2: Evaluated on a sentence-level SNLI/Pereira proxy; the paper's original context was full-length academic documents — an adaptation boundary documented in the repository.
column3: Premise-disjoint grouped holdout (3,000 test pairs / 1,015 premise groups), clustered bootstrap confidence intervals, and group-conformal coverage (93.69% group / 97.80% pair).
column4: Proposed evaluates under a stricter leakage-free grouped protocol with formal coverage guarantees.

column4: Proposed supports auditable adjudication; Paper 1 does not.

column2: Single threshold; no calibrated probabilities, uncertainty quantification, conformal coverage, budget formalization, or audit dossiers; sentence-level proxy data.
column3: Candidate recall below 1.0 on text (0.8598); group coverage 93.69% slightly below the nominal 95%; text corpus is a proxy; training time and memory not instrumented.
column4: Complementary limitation profiles: Paper 1 lacks uncertainty and audit machinery; the proposed framework accepts a bounded candidate-recall trade-off for cost control.
